samples.label: Bi nanocrystal seed cohort characterized in Figure 1; aliquot drying/storage state unreported
notes: Figure 1A TEM and 1B XRD characterize seeds from the stated Bi preparation before III–V nanowire growth; the paper does not identify whether those specimens were measured before or after the drying/storage step.
Drying and nitrogen storage are reported workup steps but are not proven to be the exact Figure 1 specimen state.
High-temperature and biphasic failed Bi routes lack full reagent charges and are not separate paired records.
III–V nanowire products are outside this colloidal nanocrystal package.

intuition.title: Why use TOP?
intuition.text: The authors attribute steric stabilization of room-temperature Bi seeds to TOP. They do not measure its binding geometry or surface coverage.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.2 / printed 1972, Bi Nanocrystals discussion

intuition.title: What failed in comparison routes?
intuition.text: The source reports that its alternative high-temperature and biphasic reductions gave oversized, broadly distributed or oxidized Bi. Their reagent charges are incomplete, so they are not separate paired recipes.

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
